Solution 1 is the one I judge correct, though I could not fully verify its classification, and part of this is recalled rather than derived.

**What I could check.** Take S and T with all S–T edges blue. Put a sparse red high-chromatic H₁-free graph inside S and a red complete bipartite graph inside T. Balancing degrees gives minimum degree 2n/3 with unbounded chromatic number. So every pair of 3-chromatic graphs has threshold at least 2/3. This rules out Solution 2, whose set of values includes ones below 2/3 (and its final answer 2 is unsupported). Solution 3 gives only 2/3 and 5/7 and misses the larger values.

**What I recalled but did not verify.** The set {2/3, 5/7, 3/4, 4/5} in Solution 1 matches my faint memory of the published classification. Its formula (2−d)/(3−2d) with d ∈ {0, 1/3, 1/2} gives 2/3, 5/7 and 3/4. The value 4/5 comes from the pentagon-blowup construction. Its sum is 2/3 + 5/7 + 3/4 + 4/5 = 1231/420. I could not independently confirm the classification, so this choice rests partly on that memory.

CHOICE: 1
